title: Commission urges fast rollout of age verification app (Recommendation (EU) 2026/1035)
date_evidence: Commission urges fast rollout of age verification app ... 2026-04-29 ... On 29 April 2026, the European Commission published its Recommendation for a common approach for EU-wide age verification technologies
key_claim: On 29 April 2026 the Commission adopted a non-binding Recommendation (EU) 2026/1035 for a common approach to EU-wide age verification, urging Member States to make age verification available to all users by the end of 2026; it provides an open-source age-verification app and an EU blueprint that can be adapted nationally and integrated with European Digital Identity Wallets, with privacy-preserving proof-of-age and conformity through independent assessment.
notes: Tier 1; the EU instrument that wires age verification to the Digital Identity Wallet - core of the identity-layer thesis.

title: The Commission, Australia's eSafety Commissioner, and UK's Ofcom share insights on age assurance measures
date_evidence: NEWS ARTICLE Publication 03 February 2026 ... On 3 February 2026, the Commission, the eSafety Commissioner and Ofcom's cooperation group on age assurance
key_claim: On 3 February 2026 the cooperation group of the European Commission, Australia's eSafety Commissioner and the UK's Ofcom (formed under a November 2025 Joint communication) held its first meeting; Australia's enforcement of its under-16 social media restrictions has already seen platforms remove access to around 4.7 million accounts identified as belonging to children under 16, and the three regulators will hold regular exchanges through 2026 on age-assurance approaches and enforcement.
notes: Tier 1; cross-jurisdiction regulatory convergence and the 4.7m Australian accounts figure.

title: Keep underage children off your platforms, Ofcom tells tech firms
date_evidence: Keep underage children off your platforms Ofcom tells tech firms 12032026153000 ... On 12 March 2026, Ofcom ... deadline of 30 April to report back
key_claim: On 12 March 2026 Ofcom wrote to Facebook, Instagram, Roblox, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube setting out four demands, including using 'highly effective age assurance' to enforce minimum-age rules, with a deadline of 30 April 2026 to report back; Ofcom's research finds 72% of children aged 8-12 still access sites and apps with a minimum age of 13.
notes: Tier 1; UK enforcement turn with a hard 30 April 2026 deadline and the 72% under-age-access figure.

title: ISO/IEC 27566-1:2025 - Age assurance systems - Part 1: Framework
date_evidence: ISO/IEC 27566-1:2025 ... Age assurance systems - Part 1: Framework ... Edition 1 ... publication date December 2025
key_claim: ISO and IEC published ISO/IEC 27566-1:2025, the first international standard establishing a framework for age assurance systems (developed under ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 27), defining core concepts - age verification, age estimation, age inference and successive validation - for age-related eligibility decisions; the European Commission, ITU and the Age Verification Providers Association petitioned to make it freely available.
notes: Tier 1 structural anchor (Dec 2025, ~6 months): the canonical international standard underpinning the standards-convergence thesis. One anchor permitted.

title: The EU Commission's Approach to Age Verification: Mobile Apps, DSA Enforcement, and Challenging National Social Media Bans
date_evidence: The EU Commission's Approach to Age Verification ... May 12, 2026 ... Last Updated: May 12, 2026
key_claim: The EU's age-verification Recommendation envisages a blueprint (an open-source mobile app and technical specification) consistent with the EU Digital Identity Wallet, and a 'scheme' for proof-of-age attestations from a list of EU-based trusted providers with conformity assessment reminiscent of the EU AI Act's product-safety approach; whether age verification is mandatory or voluntary under the DSA remains legally unsettled, the Commission did not reference the GDPR, and the early-April EU 'age-checking app' was reportedly broken by hackers within minutes.
notes: Tier 2 think-tank analysis; the load-bearing source for the 'identity layer' and the mandatory-vs-voluntary counter-argument.

title: The EU's Age Verification Efforts: Child Protection, Privacy, and Digital Identity
date_evidence: The EU's Age Verification Efforts ... As of 11 May 2026, 23 of 27 EU member states were at least considering national legislation
key_claim: As of 11 May 2026, 23 of 27 EU member states were at least considering national legislation on minors' social-media access, but approaches differ significantly in age thresholds, enforcement models and covered services; without consensus on what counts as 'social media', member states may regulate different services and adopt divergent models, complicating an 'EU-wide' framework.
notes: Tier 2; the fragmentation evidence (23/27 member states, divergent models) - supports both the spread and the counter-argument.

title: Age assurance regulation for social media to go global in 2026
date_evidence: Age assurance regulation for social media to go global in 2026 ... biometricupdate.com/202601/ ... Australia's law ... took effect on December 10 ... Jordan has given Inman Grant until January 13, 2026
key_claim: Following Australia's under-16 ban (effective 10 December 2025), France (under-15, by September 2026), Ireland, Spain and Germany are advancing age-assurance laws, with the next stage of testing tied to the new ISO/IEC 27566-1 standard; meanwhile the US is pushing back hard, with NetChoice litigation, First Amendment arguments and the Trump administration imposing visa bans on European online-safety officials and threatening Australia's eSafety Commissioner with contempt.
notes: Tier 3 trade press; the global-spread map and the US political/legal pushback for the counter-argument.

title: Apple updates Declared Age Range API for national, state-level age assurance laws
date_evidence: Apple updates Declared Age Range API ... biometricupdate.com/202602/ ... Apple released a beta update to its Declared Age Range API on February 25, 2026 ... As of February 24, 2026, Apple began blocking ... apps rated 18+ in Brazil, Australia, and Singapore
key_claim: On 25 February 2026 Apple released a beta update to its Declared Age Range API to help developers meet age-assurance obligations under laws in Brazil, Australia, Singapore, Utah and Louisiana; from 24 February 2026 Apple began blocking 18+ app downloads in Brazil, Australia and Singapore unless adulthood is confirmed, with Utah (6 May 2026) and Louisiana (1 July 2026) to follow; the API returns a device-level age-range signal and the method of age assurance.
notes: Tier 3 reporting on the OS-level architecture shift (device-emitted age signals) at the heart of the identity-layer thesis.
